rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Warm != referent-present — walk each definite reference in the fence.
rules_evaluated.evidence: compound-and-close-1's fence opens 'Review this session end-to-end: the orientation and introspection, the /context read, the TDD bug fix, the diff push-back.' Three of the four referents are genuine prior turns in the same session's scrollback. The fourth, 'the /context read', names the slash command '/context' run in the prior exercise. WebFetch of code.claude.com/docs/en/commands (2026-08-01) describes /context as a client-side visualization ('Visualize current context usage as a colored grid') with no documented signal that its invocation or output becomes model-visible conversation text — i.e. Claude reviewing 'this session end-to-end' later may have no actual memory of that turn. Docs-derived, not live-tested (per check_platform_and_boundaries.md #5a's negative-claim corollary, this is flagged as live-probe-owed, not asserted as certain fact). Low practical impact: one clause in a four-item recap list; the other three referents give Claude ample real material to write the rules file from.
rules_evaluated.fix_hint: Live-probe: run /context in a real session, then ask a later turn what it showed. If confirmed invisible to the model, either drop '/context read' from the recap clause or have the student explicitly narrate the reading back to Claude in chat so it lands in scrollback.
